texts.preamble: Sandeep Satish Jaiswal vs The State Of Maharashtra on 12 February, 2019 Author: V.K. Jadhav Bench: V.K. Jadhav 1 Aba 64.2019.odt In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Anticipatory Bail Application No.64 Of 2019 Sandeep Satish Jaiswal Versus The State Of Maharashtra ... Advocate for Applicant : Mr A K Bhosale App for Respondent : Mr A P Basarkar ... Coram : V.K. Jadhav, J. Dated : February 12, 2019 ... Per Court :- 1. The applicant is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with Crime No.0404 of 2018 registered at Ambad Police Station, Tq. Ambad, District Jalna, for the offences punishable under sections 188, 272, 273, 328 of Indian Penal Code and u/s 59 of the Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006.

texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is the driver of the vehicle Nano and Sandeep Satish Jaiswal vs The State Of Maharashtra on 12 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33805674/ 1 aaa/- ::: Uploaded on - 12/02/2019 ::: Downloaded on - 13/02/2019 03:14:40 : : : 2 ABA 64.2019.odt he has no knowledge about the goods under transportation. He was simply obeying the directions of employers. Learned counsel submits that, except the offence under section 328 of the IPC, other offences are bailable. So far as offence under section 328 of IPC is concerned, the same is not attracted since the applicant has no specific intention to cause hurt to any person. Thus, there is hardly any evidence with regard to the provisions of section 188 and 328 of IPC. Learned counsel submits that since the applicant is the driver and the contraband articles were already seized from the vehicle, his custodial interrogation is not required. He may be released on anticipatory bail. 3. Learned APP has strongly resisted the application on the ground huge quantity of contraband articles are seized.
